title: Chapter 127 — Email & Written Communication
intro: Every email you send is a permanent record of your professionalism.

sections.title: Email Standards
sections.content:
Response time: within 4 hours during business hours. Subject lines should be clear and specific — 'Your Bosch dishwasher quote — valid through Friday' not 'Following up.' Lead with the action item or answer. Use their name. Keep it concise.

Proofread everything. One typo in a $10,000 quote makes you look careless. A model number error costs real money. Read every email twice before sending — especially the ones with numbers.

sections.title: Tone in Writing
sections.content:
Write with a professional tone without sounding robotic. 'Hi Sarah, great talking with you today' is better than 'Dear Ms. Smith, per our discussion.' Match the customer's tone — if they write casually, respond casually. If they write formally, mirror that.

When handling complaints in writing, never match anger. A calm, solution-focused email defuses more tension than a defensive one. 'I understand your frustration about the delivery delay. Here is what I am doing to fix it right now.'

sections.title: Know When to Call Instead
sections.content:
Some conversations should not happen over email. Complaints — call. Bad news about delays or discontinuations — call. Complex technical discussions — call. Anything where tone could be misread — call.

Email is for information delivery, confirmations, and follow-ups. Phone is for relationship-building, problem-solving, and anything emotionally charged.
